trials.title: NumPy full-budget gate report construction
trials.description: Reduces metal sulfide and full curated runtime by moving full-condensate budget gate report construction from many small JAX operations to NumPy without changing the gate formula, solver math, support retry policy, or acceptance thresholds.

cprofile.finding: The target layer profile showed many small JAX cache-miss/compile and materialization costs around public report/gate construction.

trials.verdict: The first speed improvement reduces the targeted metal sulfide runtime surface by about 28% while keeping the v1.18 curated public score, routes, and acceptance tiers unchanged.

trials.title: Cached NumPy formula matrices and dense vector assembly
trials.description: Reduces repeated Python-side report/restoration overhead by caching immutable setup formula matrices as NumPy arrays and avoiding small JAX scatter/update operations when assembling full condensate vectors.

implementation.cache_policy: weakref-backed cache keyed by setup object identity

trials.verdict: Caching immutable setup formula matrices and avoiding small JAX scatter/update operations gives a smaller but measurable second speedup while keeping the v1.18 public route, status, and tier surface unchanged.

trials.title: Opt-in condensate profile initializers and previous-layer warm starts
trials.description: Adds a condensate profile API surface that supports independent per-layer initializers, future grid-backed initializers, and sequential previous-layer warm starts. Runtime measurements show scan hot starts are family-dependent, so the default remains independent per-layer execution.
trials.verdict: Previous-layer warm starts are useful as an opt-in profile method. scan_hot_from_bottom is faster on the curated aggregate and selected families such as metal sulfide benefit strongly from scan_hot_from_top, but route/status/tier changes make scan hot starts unsuitable as the global default. The API supports both sequential previous-layer initialization and independent grid-style per-layer initialization without changing existing one-layer defaults.

trials.title: BVLS bounded least-squares full-budget polish
trials.description: Reduces remaining Python-side support restoration overhead by using SciPy BVLS for the bounded support-amount polish problem. Profiling showed this path dominated representative heavy layers after the earlier report and formula-cache speedups.

implementation.rejected_experiment: Replacing the square PD-IPM lstsq solve with np.linalg.solve increased inner iterations on metal-sulfide layers and was reverted.

trials.verdict: BVLS is a safe default for the bounded support-amount polish path. It reduces the order-matched all-curated fast-monotone runtime by about 14% while keeping the PD-IPM iteration surface and public status counts unchanged.

trials.title: remove duplicate gas solve and redundant depleted gas refresh
implementation: Skip solve_gas_equilibrium_with_duals when initial_log_state_override is provided because the gas solution is only used for the default initial state.
Skip the post-solver depleted gas refresh when the incoming override source is exogibbs_native_depleted_budget_gas_refresh.
trials.verdict: The duplicate gas solve and redundant depleted-refresh work can be removed safely. The all-curated fast-monotone score improves by about 7.2% with identical status counts and identical continuation iteration counts.

trials.title: warm explicit support-closure retry from lifecycle final gas state
implementation_attempted: Pass a CondensateEquilibriumInit built from the lifecycle final gas state into the recursive explicit_support_closure_retry call.
Then add a cold retry fallback if the warm retry is not accepted.
trials.verdict: Rejected. Warm-starting explicit support-closure retry from the previous lifecycle gas state is not a safe speed path: without fallback it breaks a closure-repair case, and with fallback it slows all-curated fast_monotone by about 10.9%.
